the endogenous lipoxins stimulate Cl− secretion and enhance airway surface liquid (ASL) in non-CF airway epithelia and also in CF airway epithelia.
LXA4 stimulates intracellular Ca2+-activated chloride channels in normal and CF bronchiali epithelial cells leading to increased ASL height.

the role of eicosanoids in the regulation of airway function in CF.
the role of LXA₄ in CF and the potential therapeutic use of LXA₅ in CF.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
LXA4 is able to stimulate Ca2+ influx and the activation of Ca2+-activated chloride currents which in turn increases ASL height in normal and cystic fibrosis epithelial cells.
LXA4 is able to stimulate Cl− secretion through Ca2+-dependent pathways in non-CF bronchial epithelium.
LXA4 stimulates Ca2+-activated chloride currents and increases airway surface liquid height in normal and cystic fibrosis airway epithelia.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the eicosanoids, LXA4 and 15-epi LXA4, have a role in the regulation of ASL height by increasing Cl− secretion in non-CF bronchial epithelium and that this effect is maintained in the bronchial epithela of patients with CF.
LXA4 is an endogenous anti-inflammatory lipid that stimulates Ca2+-dependent Cl− currents and enhances ASL height.

we have demonstrated that LXA4, via activation of ALX/FPR-2, stimulates Ca2+-activated chloride secretion in non-CF bronchial epithelium and in CF bronchial cells, which results in increased ASL height.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the endogenous lipoxins are important regulators of airway epithelia function and that the LXA4/ALX/FPR2 pathway may represent a novel therapeutic target for the management of the airway dehydration in CF.
